title: Displays "Parse Error: Busy." when typing inside a script (in specific cases)
body:
### Tested versions

v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb]

Please, note that I first noticed this on v4.7 and updated later to 4.7.1 which is the version I created the MRP on.

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - TUXEDO OS 24.04.4 LTS on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon 890M Graphics (RADV STRIX1) - AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 w/ Radeon 890M (24 threads) - 61.91 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Everything seems to work, the issue is that error messages are displayed in the output dock.

I noticed this in a personal project. To keep things simple, let's say I have, multiple "new" scenes (which are currently used in the project) but also some "old" scenes that were used in the past but not used any more (I only keep them in case I want to use them again). Errors concern "old" scenes and are only displayed for "old" scenes that are not opened in an editor tab. These error are triggered when I type in a script that has nothing to do with them. I also noticed that they are not displayed it they are referenced in a resource that is inside an opened scene.

### Steps to reproduce

**with the MRP:**
1. open the project
2. check that `old.gd` is closed (if it is open, the errors are already diplayed)
3. check that `old.tscn` is not an opened tab (if it is, close it and reload the current project)
4. open `main.gd` and type any character
5. wait less than 1s
6. you will see errors inside the output dock:
```
  ERROR: scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:293 - Parse Error: Busy. [Resource file res://old.tscn:12]
  ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://old.tscn.
  ERROR: scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:293 - Parse Error: Busy. [Resource file res://old.tscn:12]
  ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://old.tscn.
```

**from scratch:**
1. create a new project.
2. create a main scene with a script.
3. create another scene with another script (the equivalent to "old" in the MRP)
4. in the script created at step 3, drag and drop the scene main scene holding the control key. this will create a constant with a preload of the main scene.
5. close the tab of the scene created at sep 3 and its script.
6. reload the project type inside the the script of the main scene and you will see the errors.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[busy_error_reproduction_2026-07-17_17-29-24.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30135572/busy_error_reproduction_2026-07-17_17-29-24.zip)
